**Data.** There are 240 rows with 240 unique IDs, so one patient is one replicate. In total, 138 patients died of gastric cancer and the others are censored. No rows were dropped from any model.

### 1. Kaplan-Meier and log-rank test (all patients)
| MMP-14 group | n | Events | Median DSS (years) | 5-year DSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low (< 0.073 ng/ml) | 201 | 108 | 4.175 | 49.2 % (0.4923) |
| High (≥ 0.073 ng/ml) | 39 | 30 | 1.796 | 22.1 % (0.2211) |

- The log-rank test gives chi-square 10.23, df 1, p = 0.00138. This is significant at alpha 0.05.
- The tool did not give a confidence interval for the 5-year survival values.
- The figure is in `kaplan_meier-1/kaplan_meier.png`.

### 2. Cox models of disease-specific survival
- All models use Breslow ties, which come from your decision record.
- The confidence level is 95 %, which is 1 minus alpha 0.05.
- Each HR compares high with low MMP-14.

| Model | n | Events | HR for high MMP-14 | 95 % CI | p | Concordance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unadjusted, all patients | 240 | 138 | 1.92 | 1.28 to 2.88 | 0.00167 | 0.550 |
| Adjusted, all patients | 240 | 138 | 1.55 | 1.02 to 2.35 | 0.0399 | 0.800 |
| Unadjusted, intestinal type | 84 (9 high) | 37 | 3.54 | 1.51 to 8.33 | 0.00374 | 0.566 |
| Unadjusted, diffuse type | 156 (30 high) | 101 | 1.54 | 0.964 to 2.45 | 0.0711 | 0.541 |

The adjusted model has these covariates: age_ge67, stage2, stage3 and stage4 (stage 1 is the reference) and diffuse. Their HRs in that model, with 95 % CI, are:
- age_ge67: HR 2.52 (1.76 to 3.60), p = 4.4 × 10⁻⁷
- stage2: HR 6.88 (2.35 to 20.1), p = 0.00044
- stage3: HR 22.0 (7.98 to 60.8), p = 2.4 × 10⁻⁹
- stage4: HR 74.5 (25.8 to 215), p = 1.7 × 10⁻¹⁵
- diffuse: HR 2.23 (1.50 to 3.32), p = 7.3 × 10⁻⁵

In the intestinal type, the HR is significant at alpha 0.05. In the diffuse type, it is not significant at alpha 0.05.

**Proportional hazards check.** The Cox tool runs this test only with Efron ties, so the Breslow fits did not include it. I ran a separate Schoenfeld residual test (Efron fit, rank time transform) as a check. No covariate failed it in any of the four models. For high MMP-14, p was 0.6271 unadjusted, 0.8803 adjusted, 0.4823 in the intestinal type and 0.3433 in the diffuse type. The full table is in `ph_check.csv`.

- **Wide intervals.** Only 9 intestinal-type patients have a high MMP-14 (7 events), so the HR of 3.54 has a wide interval. The adjusted stage HRs also have wide intervals, because few stage 1 patients died.

- **No correction for many tests.** This answer has one log-rank test and four Cox tests for high MMP-14. All p-values are raw. No correction was requested, so none was applied.
- **Hazard ratios are not risk ratios.** An HR of 1.92 means a higher rate of death from gastric cancer over follow-up. It does not mean 1.92 times the risk.
- **Association, not cause.** These are observational data. The results show an association, not that MMP-14 causes worse survival.

- Nothing is blocked.
